transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in today? Is there something specific you'd like to talk about or get help with?

Yeah, um… I guess what brings me in is what happens after I eat like that. I mean, I’ll be sitting there, you know, with empty containers around me, and I just feel… disgusted with myself.

It’s hard to explain. I’ve always tried to be a steady guy, in control, especially with my work and all that driving, keeping schedules, dealing with people. My dad was like that too—never made a fuss, just handled things. And then I look at myself after, and it’s like… that’s not the man I thought I was.
After you've eaten like this, do you ever try to compensate by making yourself sick, exercising a lot, or anything like that?

I… I don’t really know how to answer that cleanly. I mean, I don’t sit there with some plan like, “Okay, now I have to undo this.” Mostly I just feel awful and kind of… sit with it.

I’ve never been much of an exercise guy, other than work keeping me moving, climbing in and out, loading things, that sort of thing. My knees aren’t what they used to be either—too many years on the road, I guess. As far as making myself sick… no, I don’t think that’s something I do. I just feel ashamed after, mostly.
Do you ever find yourself eating a lot more than you intended in a short period of time, like feeling like you can’t stop once you start?

Yeah… yeah, that’s probably the part that scares me most. Once I start, it’s like the same discipline I’ve had my whole life—on the road, keeping time, making deliveries, knowing when to stop for fuel and when not to—that just shuts off.

I’ll be sitting there telling myself, “Magin, put the fork down. That’s enough.” And I mean I’m really saying it in my head. But then my hand just goes back for more anyway. It’s like there’s a gap between what I know I should do and what I’m actually doing.
How often do these episodes where you feel like you can't stop eating happen? Like, is this something that happens multiple times a week, once a week, or less often?

Since I’ve been home with this back injury, it’s been… several nights most weeks, I’d say. I don’t know, the days kind of run together when you’re not out driving your regular route. Used to be I could mark a week by where I was supposed to be, who I’d see, that kind of thing.

But yeah… thinking about it, these last three months, I can’t really think of a single week where it didn’t happen at least once. Most weeks more than that. Several nights.
During these episodes, do you feel like you're losing control over how much you're eating, like you can't stop once you start?

Yeah… that’s exactly what it feels like. Like I’m losing the wheel, I guess.

I spent years on the road, and you get used to having control—watching the gauges, knowing when to stop, keeping yourself on schedule. But when this happens, once I start eating, that part of me just sort of shuts off. I’ll be telling myself, Magin, put the fork down, that’s enough, and I mean it… but my hand still goes back for more anyway. It’s like I’m watching myself do it and not stopping.
Do you often feel really guilty, upset, or embarrassed about these episodes after they happen?

Yeah… I do. That’s really what got me sitting here, if I’m honest.

Afterward I’ll just sit there and look at the empty containers or plates, and it hits me all at once. I feel disgusted with myself. Embarrassed, too, even if nobody’s standing there seeing it. It’s like… I’ve always thought of myself as a steady guy, you know? Kept my rig on schedule, kept things under control, did what needed doing. And then I’m sitting there with all that food gone, thinking, “What happened to that man?”

So yeah. Upset, guilty… all of that.
Have these episodes ever made it hard for you to function normally, like affecting your work or relationships, or making you avoid social situations because of how you feel afterward?

Yeah… it has. Not so much work-work right now, since I’m not out on the route, but the people from work, that’s where I notice it.

There are a couple of younger drivers I was supposed to be kind of checking in on, mentoring a little. Usually I’d take those calls no problem—talk about routes, paperwork, which loading docks are a pain, all that. I used to like feeling useful that way. Reminded me of when older guys showed me the ropes, back when half of it was still paper maps and pay phones, you know?

But lately I see their names come up and I just… let it ring. Or I’ll tell myself I’ll call them back later and then I don’t. I feel ashamed, like if they hear my voice they’ll somehow know how far off my routine I’ve gotten. Like I’m not the guy they should be asking for advice anymore. So yeah, I’ve been avoiding those calls because of how I feel afterward.
Do you usually eat alone during these episodes because you're embarrassed about how much you're eating?

I’m not sure I could say “usually” in a clean way. I mean… a lot of times I’m by myself just because that’s how my day is set up, you know? Years of being on the road, eating in the cab or grabbing something where nobody’s really paying attention to you anyway.

The embarrassed part… yeah, that’s in there, I guess, but I don’t know if I’m planning it like, “I need to hide.” It’s more like I don’t want anybody around asking, “You really gonna eat all that?” Reminds me of being at truck stops where everybody’s half-watching everybody but pretending they aren’t.

So… I don’t know. I do end up alone a lot, but I can’t say I’ve kept track of whether it’s because I’m embarrassed or just because that’s how it happens.
Do you find yourself feeling very upset or preoccupied about your body shape or weight during or after these eating episodes?

I don’t know if I’d put it that way, exactly. I mean, I know I’m not twenty-five anymore, and my belt tells me plenty without me needing a lecture, you know? But during those times, I’m not really thinking, “Oh, my body shape,” or anything that clear.

Afterward… I might feel bad, sure, but I don’t know that it’s specifically about weight. It’s more just… I don’t know, the whole situation. Like when you’re hauling a load and you know something shifted but you haven’t opened the trailer yet—you can just feel it’s not right. Sorry, that’s probably not answering it clean.

So, no, I haven’t really noticed being very focused on body shape or weight during or after. Not in a way I could point to.
During or after these eating episodes, do you feel particularly distressed or anxious specifically about the large amount of food you've eaten?

Yeah… that part, yes. Maybe not in the middle of it so much, because then I’m just kind of… doing it. But after, when it’s quiet, I’ll see all the empty containers there, wrappers or whatever, and it hits me.

I get this disgusted feeling with myself. Not just “oh, I ate too much,” but like… what happened to me? I’ve always tried to be a steady guy, you know, the kind of man who keeps control of himself, does what he says he’s gonna do. Like in driving, you check your mirrors, keep your lane, don’t make sudden moves—sorry, I know that’s not exactly what you asked.

But yeah. Afterward I feel pretty bad about the amount. I sit there looking at it and I feel ashamed, like I let myself down.
